text:
aditya: FYI customer Acorn just opened an escalation — sudden p95/p99 spike on Dedicated pool during billing window, ~30% requests hitting >2s p95 and p99s around 6s. They also saw attach auth 401s right before the spike.

lina: Thanks, can you paste the customer request IDs or sample traces? Which pool?

aditya: pool=dedicated-eu-west-3-acorn-minpool=2, reserve policy=burst. sample req: req-2026-03-15-09:12:47. Logs show attach attempts failing with 401 from attach-service, then retries that succeed and cause long warmup.

aditya: snippet from attach logs: 
```
[09:12:46] attach-request req-2026-03-15-09:12:47 token=xxxx status=401 auth-service: invalid-token
[09:12:47] attach-request retry token=yyyy status=200 attached gpu-03
[09:12:47] start-model-load gpu-03 model=redwood-7b quant=4bit
[09:12:50] first-token 95th=2200ms
```

tom: Interesting — two things to triage: (1) auth failures during attach -> could be token rotation edge-case, (2) attach retries triggering cold GPU startup which amplifies p99.

maya: Is this limited to Acorn or broader? Alerting shows small bump in EU dedicated pools at same time but Acorn's traffic pattern (burst at billing boundary) pushed their pool to scale beyond minpool and hit coldstarts.

srebot: automated-alert: dedicated-eu-west-3 - scaleup_latency_p99=6.2s (threshold 2.5s) - 09:12 UTC.

lina: Repro steps we should try: 1) simulate attach/auth 401 for a subset of requests, 2) force retry path to attach and measure warmup timings, 3) validate token refresh logic in attach-service client.

tom: I'm going to pull auth-service logs for that timeframe — looking for 401 causes (expired token vs missing claims).

(aditya uploads a short trace link)

aditya: trace: https://redwood-traces/internal/trace/req-2026-03-15-09-12-47

maya: From traces I see attach-service returned 401 for ~12 requests in a short window, most with header x-kms-key-id mismatch. Could be a KMS rotate window where cached key not refreshed.

lina: That matches one hypothesis: if attach fails, client retries with different token and attaches to a fresh GPU -> triggers model load and warmup. Multiple concurrent retries cause several GPUs to start loading at once -> saturation + queueing -> p99 spike.

tom: Mitigations to consider immediately: - increase minpool for suspect customers during known billing windows - add jitter/randomized backoff to attach retry logic - short-circuit known transient 401s with a quick token-refresh path rather than full retry flow.

aditya: Customer asked for workaround now. Can we suggest increasing minpool to 4 for Acorn and enable prewarm policy for billing-window 09:00-09:15?

maya: We can apply minpool change via console; will need ops-ok for immediate change. Also can toggle proactive warmup flag for that pool.

lina: I'll open a short-lived runbook: set minpool=4, set warmup-window=09:00-09:20, shorten attach retry backoff from exponential to 100ms jitter base for 2 minutes. That should reduce concurrent cold starts.

tom: On auth side, we should check attach-client's token caching TTL. I see code in attach-client: 
```
token = cache.get('attach_token')
if token.expired: token = kms.sign(new_payload)
retry_count += 1
```
We might be hitting a race where multiple processes observe token expired and request new signed tokens with different KMS key versions. Need to guard with singleflight or short mutex.

maya: Agreed. Quick fix: add singleflight/lock in attach-client to serialize token refresh for short window. Longer fix: ensure KMS key rotation and cache invalidation is coordinated.

srebot: incident-note: initial mitigation applied: minpool bumped to 4 and proactive warmup enabled for dedicated-eu-west-3-acorn at 09:38 UTC.

aditya: After minpool bump and warmup enabled, customer reports p99 dropped to ~1.1s for subsequent burst. They confirmed no more auth 401s in 09:40 burst.

lina: Action items: 1) eng-platform to add singleflight to attach-client token refresh (P0), 2) infra/ops to verify KMS rotate logs and ensure no overlapping key versions (P1), 3) support to propose prewarm schedules for customers with known billing window bursts (P2).

tom: I'll file the attach-client change PR and tag eng-runtime for review. Draft title: "serialize attach token refresh to avoid stampeding attach retries".

maya: Also add monitoring: alert when attach 401 rate > 0.5% for more than 1m on a pool so we can auto-prewarm or notify support earlier.

aditya: Customer happy for now, moving to post-incident notes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

lina: I'll write up a short postmortem and include timeline + logs + suggested fixes. Will attach to ticket #AC-4921.

tom: +1. Closing thread unless something else pops up.
